facts.text: Persepolis was the capital of the Iranian Empire; a pillar from Persepolis is similar to an Ashokan Pillar.
facts.quote: The image on the left shows a pillar from Persepolis, the capital of the Iranian Empire, while the image on the right shows an Ashokan Pillar.

facts.text: India shared close relations with Central Asia, Iran (Persia), China, Tibet, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Indonesia.
facts.quote: India shared close relation with countries in Central Asia, Iran (Persia), China, Tibet, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Indonesia.

facts.text: Ancient India and Persia had cultural, commercial and political relations from ancient times.
facts.quote: Ancient India and Persia had cultural, commercial and political relations from ancient times.

facts.text: The northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent (Gandhara and Sindh) formed a part of the Persian Empire.
facts.quote: The northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent (Gandhara and Sindh) formed a part of the Persian Empire.

facts.text: The Persian Empire was known as the 'Achaemenid Empire'; it was divided into provinces, and taxation, intelligence network and hierarchy of officials were based on this division.
facts.quote: The Persian Empire was known as the 'Achaemenid Empire'. It was divided into different provinces. The structure of taxation, intelligence network and the hierarchy of officials was decided, based on this division.

facts.text: The administrative system of the Mauryan empire shows some influence of the Persian administrative system.
facts.quote: The administrative system of the Mauryan empire shows some influence of the Persian administrative system.

facts.text: The Persian Empire had spread up to Rome.
facts.quote: The Persian Empire had spread up to Rome.

facts.text: The Kharoshthi and Aramaic scripts used in some Ashokan inscriptions indicate Persian influence.
facts.quote: The Kharoshthi and Aramaic scripts used in some of the Ashokan inscriptions indicate Persian influence.

facts.text: India exported textiles, pearls, spices and elephants to Persia; precious metals were imported from Persia.
facts.quote: India exported textiles, pearls, spices and elephants, to Persia. Precious metals were imported from Persia.

facts.text: Persian influence is seen in the capitals of Ashokan pillars, which have figures of animals like lion, horse and bull.
facts.quote: The influence of Persian art and architecture is clearly seen in the capitals of Ashokan pillars, which have figures of animals like lion, horse and bull.

facts.text: In 326 BCE, Alexander, the King of Macedonia, conquered Persia and marched towards the northwestern region of India.
facts.quote: In 326 BCE, Alexander, the King of Macedonia, conquered Persia and marched towards the northwestern region of India.

facts.text: Alexander brought small kingdoms in the Indus region under his control; after his death his empire broke into small Indo-Greek kingdoms.
facts.quote: He brought several small kingdoms in the Indus region under his control. After Alexander's death, his empire was disintegrated in small kingdoms. These are known as Indo-Greek kingdoms.

facts.text: The Mauryan emperors Chandragupta, Bindusara and Ashoka established political relations with Greek kings.
facts.quote: The Mauryan emperors Chandragupta, Bindusara and Ashoka established political relations with Greek kings.

facts.text: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador in Chandragupta Maurya's court; he wrote Indica, about the social structure, administration, agriculture and trade of the Mauryan period.
facts.quote: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador in Chandragupta Maurya's court. He wrote Indica, a book that provides valuable information about the social structure, administration, agriculture, and trade of the Mauryan period.

facts.text: 'Gandhara Art' emerged during the Kushana period; it was influenced by Greek sculptural traditions, and many images of Gautam Buddha are in this style.
facts.quote: A new school of art emerged in India during the Kushana period. It is known as 'Gandhara Art'. It was influenced by Greek sculptural traditions. A number of images of Gautam Buddha in Gandhara style are found. Faces of Gandhara sculptures resemble Greek facial features.

facts.text: Coins minted by the Greek kings of Bactria are called 'Indo-Greek coins'.
facts.quote: The coins minted by the Greek kings of Bactria are excellent examples of this art form. These coins are called as 'Indo-Greek coins'.

facts.text: During the 1st and 2nd centuries CE, trade between India and Rome flourished; the ports of South India were important.
facts.quote: During the 1st and 2nd centuries CE, trade between India and Rome flourished. In this trade-network, the ports of South India were important.

facts.text: Bronze objects of Roman make were found at Kolhapur in Maharashtra, and many things of Roman origin at Arikamedu in Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: During the excavations at Kolhapur in Maharashtra bronze objects of Roman make were found. Similarly, many things of Roman origin were found during excavations at Arikamedu in Tamil Nadu.

facts.text: Ter, in the Dharashiv district of Maharashtra, was an important centre of Indo-Roman trade in the Satavahan period.
facts.quote: Ter was an important trade centre of Indo-Roman trade in the Satavahan period. It is located in the Dharashiv district of Maharashtra.

facts.text: Excavations at Ter yielded Roman coins, amphorae, glass beads and ivory carvings, including an ivory doll measuring 12 centimetres.
facts.quote: Excavations at this site have yielded Roman coins, amphorae (storage jars), glass beads and ivory carvings. ... an ivory doll measuring 12-centimeters, draws special attention.

facts.text: A similar ivory doll was found at Pompeii, a city in Italy buried in a volcanic eruption in 79 CE.
facts.quote: Similar ivory doll was found at Pompeii. This historical city in Italy was buried in a volcanic eruption in 79 CE.

facts.text: The port of Alexandria in Egypt played a crucial role; Arab merchants took Indian goods to Alexandria, from where they were shipped to Europe.
facts.quote: The port of Alexandria in Egypt played a crucial role in this trade network. Arab merchants took Indian goods to Alexandria. These goods were shipped to various European nations from Alexandria.

facts.text: Some Roman merchants travelled directly to India via South Indian ports; thousands of Roman coins are still found in India's coastal regions.
facts.quote: Some Roman merchants would travel directly to India via the South Indian ports ... Even today, thousands of Roman coins are found in India's coastal regions.

facts.text: Black pepper from India was so expensive in Rome that it was called 'Black Gold'; it was exported from South Indian ports and paid for in gold coins.
facts.quote: In Rome, it was so expensive that it was referred as 'Black Gold'. ... Pepper was exported in large quantities from ports in South India to the Roman Empire. Roman merchants would buy pepper from Indian traders by paying them in gold coins.

facts.text: The Roman writer Pliny wrote: 'Every year, a massive amount of gold flows out of Rome to get spices from India'.
facts.quote: The Roman writer Pliny records in his writings: "Every year, a massive amount of gold flows out of Rome to get spices from India".

facts.text: India's influence spread to Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia.
facts.quote: led to spread India's influence to regions including Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia.

facts.text: The Angkorwat temple and the Borobudur Stupa are strong examples of Indian influence in Southeast Asia.
facts.quote: Beautiful structures such as the Angkorwat temple, the Borobudur Stupa, and art inspired by the Indian epics stand as strong examples of this influence.

facts.text: To spread Buddhism, Emperor Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka; both are mentioned in the 'Mahavamsa'.
facts.quote: To spread Buddhism, Emperor Ashoka sent his son, Mahendra, and his daughter, Sanghamitra, to Sri Lanka. The names of both of them are mentioned in the 'Mahavamsa', a Buddhist treatise from Sri Lanka.

facts.text: Sanghamitra carried a branch of the Bodhi tree; according to local tradition it became the Bodhi tree at Anuradhpur.
facts.quote: Sanghamitra carried a branch of the Bodhi tree with her. According to local tradition, it is that branch which has turned into the Bodhi tree at Anuradhpur.

facts.text: There was great demand in India for pearls and other precious raw material from Sri Lanka.
facts.quote: There was a great demand in India for pearls and other precious raw material from Sri Lanka.

facts.text: At Sigiriya in Sri Lanka, King Kashyapa excavated the cave in the 5th century CE; its murals are similar to the Ajanta murals.
facts.quote: At the site of Sigiriya in Sri Lanka, a king named Kashyapa excavated the cave during the 5th century CE. The style of the murals in these caves is similar to the murals in Ajanta caves.

facts.text: 'Mahavamsa' and 'Dipavamsa', Sri Lankan treatises in the Pali language, give information on India-Sri Lanka relations.
facts.quote: 'Mahavamsa' and 'Dipavamsa', the Sri Lankan treatises written in the Pali language, provide information regarding the mutual relations between India and Sri Lanka.

facts.text: Emperor Harshavardhana had sent a representative to the Chinese imperial court.
facts.quote: Emperor Harshavardhana had sent a representative to the Chinese imperial court.

facts.text: Silk fabric produced in China was known in India as 'Chinanshuka'; Indian merchants exported it to the West via land-routes.
facts.quote: Silk fabric produced in China was known in India by the name 'Chinanshuka'. ... Merchants in ancient India used to export it to countries in the West. This trade was conducted via land-routes.

facts.text: The route that passed through India, Afghanistan and Central Asia is known as the 'Silk Route'.
facts.quote: The route that passed through India, Afghanistan and Central Asia is known as the 'Silk Route'.

facts.text: Nalasopara in the Palghar district, near Mumbai, was a city on the Silk Route.
facts.quote: Several historical cities in India were located on the Silk Route. One of them was Nalasopara in the Palghar district, near Mumbai in Maharashtra.

facts.text: The Buddhist monks Fa Hien and Yuan Chwang arrived in India via the Silk Route.
facts.quote: The Buddhist monks Fa Hien and Yuan Chwang also arrived in India via the Silk Route.

facts.text: In the first century CE, at the invitation of Chinese Emperor 'Ming', the monks Dharmarakshit and Kashyapa Matanga went to China and translated Indian Buddhist texts into Chinese.
facts.quote: In the first century CE, at the invitation of the Chinese Emperor 'Ming', the Buddhist monks Dharmarakshit and Kashyapa Matanga travelled to China. They translated many Indian Buddhist texts into the Chinese language.

facts.text: Buddhism also spread to countries such as Japan, Korea and Vietnam.
facts.quote: Buddhism also spread to countries such as Japan, Korea, and Vietnam.

facts.text: In the seventh century CE, Yuan Chwang, a Buddhist monk from China, came to India and studied at Nalanda University for many years.
facts.quote: In the seventh century CE, Yuan Chwang a scholarly Buddhist monk from China arrived in India to pursue studies in Buddhism. He continued his studies at the Nalanda University for many years.

facts.text: Yuan Chwang returned to China with over 600 manuscripts, travelling by the desert route of Central Asia.
facts.quote: When he returned to China he had over 600 manuscripts with him. ... Yuan Chwang travelled by the desert route of Central Asia.

facts.text: While crossing the Taklamakan Desert, Yuan Chwang was caught in a sandstorm, but every manuscript was intact.
facts.quote: One day, while he was crossing the Taklamakan Desert, the sky suddenly turned dark. Within no time, a massive sandstorm engulfed him. ... Fortunately, every single manuscript was intact.

facts.text: The Emperor of China set up a special centre for translating Indian texts; Yuan Chwang himself translated more than seventy-five Buddhist texts into Chinese.
facts.quote: Emperor of China, welcomed Yuan Chwang and established a special centre dedicated to translating the Indian texts and manuscripts. Over the following years, Yuan Chwang himself translated more than seventy-five Buddhist texts into Chinese.

facts.text: The kingdom of 'Funan' in present-day Cambodia was established in the first century CE, founded by an Indian named Kaundinya; a Sanskrit inscription from that period still exists there.
facts.quote: The historical kingdom of 'Funan' located in present-day Cambodia, was established in the first century CE. According to Chinese historical traditions, this kingdom was founded by an Indian named Kaundinya. ... An inscription from that period still exists there. It is written in Sanskrit.

facts.text: The 'Srivijaya' Empire in Indonesia was an important centre for studying Buddhist texts and learning Sanskrit.
facts.quote: the 'Srivijaya' Empire in Indonesia was an important centre for the study of Buddhist texts and for learning Sanskrit.

facts.text: I-tsing, a Chinese traveller, went to Indonesia in 671 CE on a Persian merchant ship and stayed in Srivijaya for six months to learn Sanskrit.
facts.quote: I-tsing, a Chinese traveller went to Indonesia in 671 CE. He boarded a Persian merchant ship returning back from China. At that time, he stayed in the Srivijaya Kingdom for six months to learn Sanskrit.

facts.text: I-tsing advised Chinese monks to stay in Srivijaya for one to two years to master Sanskrit; around one thousand monks lived in its viharas.
facts.quote: I-tsing advised Chinese monks to first stay in the Srivijaya Kingdom for one to two years to master Sanskrit before proceeding to India. According to him, around one thousand monks resided in the viharas in the Srivijaya Kingdom.

facts.text: Even today in Indonesia, dance-dramas based on the Ramayana and Mahabharata are highly popular.
facts.quote: Even today in Indonesia, dance-dramas based on stories from Ramayana and Mahabharata are highly popular.

facts.text: Buddhism reached Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia in the ancient period; later, temples dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu were also built.
facts.quote: Buddhism reached countries such as Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia in the the ancient period. Later, temples dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu were also built.
